written.myAnswer: Oxidation-reduction reactions transfer electrons and hydrogen during cellular respiration. This releases energy that cells capture in ATP.

ATP means adenosine triphosphate and ADP means adenosine diphosphate. ATP supplies energy for cellular activities; when it loses a phosphate group it becomes ADP and releases energy. Energy can be used to add a phosphate group to ADP to form ATP again.
The main purpose of cellular respiration is to release energy from food and make it available to the cell, mainly in the form of ATP.
Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (ATP).
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain. It combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water, allowing aerobic respiration to continue.
Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen; anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen.
In animals, anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid. In yeast, it produces ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide.
When oxygen is insufficient during intense exercise, skeletal muscles respire anaerobically and convert pyruvic acid into lactic acid.

Energy from respiration is used for muscle contraction and movement, active transport, synthesis of molecules, cell division, transmission of nerve impulses, maintaining body temperature, and other cellular activities.

Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air through stomata in their leaves. They absorb water from the soil through their roots, and it is transported to the leaves. Carbon dioxide and water are used in photosynthesis.

Anaerobic respiration takes place without oxygen and releases less energy than aerobic respiration. Alcoholic fermentation, found in yeast, converts pyruvic acid into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide; lactic acid fermentation, found in animal muscles, converts pyruvic acid into lactic acid. It provides energy when oxygen is unavailable and fermentation is used in making foods and drinks such as bread, yogurt, cheese and alcohol.

Aerobic respiration proceeds through glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into two pyruvic acid molecules, producing ATP and NADH. Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl coenzyme-A and then oxidized in the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix, producing carbon dioxide, ATP, NADH and FADH₂. NADH and FADH₂ carry electrons to the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membrane. The energy released as electrons pass along the chain is used to make ATP; oxygen accepts electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.

Photosynthesis is an anabolic process that stores energy by making food from carbon dioxide and water, using light energy; it occurs in chloroplasts of photosynthetic organisms. Respiration is a catabolic process that breaks down food and transfers its energy to ATP; it occurs in cells and takes place continuously. Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, whereas respiration uses oxygen and releases carbon dioxide.

ATP has three phosphate groups. Its terminal phosphate can be removed to form ADP and inorganic phosphate, releasing energy for cellular work. Energy from respiration can be used to add a phosphate to ADP and reform ATP.
